new_entities.name: Glycemic control in type 2 diabetes
new_entities.description: Markers of glycemic control in type 2 diabetes, especially glycated hemoglobin and related measures of glucose regulation.

edges.effect_quant: The strongest pooled evidence shows a small HbA1c improvement with CPAP in OSA plus type 2 diabetes (MD -0.24%), but individual trials are inconsistent: one 64-patient RCT was null in intention-to-treat analysis, while smaller adherent cohorts showed larger reductions.
edges.population: adults with obstructive sleep apnea and type 2 diabetes
edges.mechanism: By reducing sleep fragmentation and intermittent hypoxemia, CPAP may improve insulin sensitivity, neurohormonal stress, and nocturnal glucose dysregulation, though the effect depends heavily on adherence and baseline glycemic burden.
edges.summary: This edge belongs in the mixed bucket. CPAP may modestly improve HbA1c in OSA with type 2 diabetes, but the effect is small and not uniformly reproduced across randomized analyses.
edges.caveats: Benefits appear more likely with longer nightly use, higher baseline HbA1c, and stable background diabetes therapy. Short trials and medication changes can easily overwhelm the signal.

evidence.citation: HerthJ et al 2023 Eur Respir Rev
evidence.notes: Effects of continuous positive airway pressure therapy on glucose metabolism in patients with obstructive sleep apnoea and type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

evidence.notes: CPAP therapy for patients with sleep apnea and type 2 diabetes mellitus improves control of blood pressure. HbA1c was unchanged in intention-to-treat analysis, with per-protocol benefit among completers.
